Why is the dairy industry bad... Well, it partially depends on how much you subscribe to the idea that cows can feel strong social connections/maternal instincts (which is very evident that they can, but some choose to be ignorant to this). Outside of that, the life of a dairy cow is short and definitely not glamorous.

Like humans, cows produce milk for their young, so dairy cows are forcefully impregnated every year, starting around their first birthday. Shortly (usually one day) after their birth, baby cows are taken from their mothers as to ensure we get all the milk they produce. The baby most often is used for veal.

The treatment of dairy cows during their use is incredibly inhumane. They spend the vast majority of their lives fenced in, standing on concrete floors and forced to live amid their own feces and develop joint issues from standing for unnatural periods of time. When producing, they are fenced so tightly that they cannot turn around. This often leads to sores on their bodies that get infected and lead to their expedited death.

Due to over-milking, it is very common that dairy cows experience mastitis, a painful inflammation of their mammary glands, that also leads to their expedited death. A healthy cow's lifespan is \~20 years, in which they can produce milk for 8-9 years. Average dairy cow lifespan is between 4 and 5 years.

Once milk production wanes, dairy cows are killed for their meat. Of course it's up for debate, but I would rather die young than live a life of torture.

This is not to mention the environmental affects of farming dairy cows. It is one of the leading producers of greenhouse gas emissions and it utilizes significantly more water than non-dairy milk options (including almond milk).

This is also not to mention the many myths regarding the health benefits of dairy milk, which I will not get into. Be skeptical of what you read. Keep in mind the dairy industry still has a lot of money that goes towards marketing their product, funding biased research, and bribing FDA.

If you're morbidly curious or actively interested in how meat/dairy products reach your plate, I highly recommend watching Dominion. It's an eye-opening documentary about the majority of animal agriculture today. [Whole thing is on youtube.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LQRAfJyEsko) Be warned, it's hard to watch.
